core_concepts: Structured thinking starts with the claim that complex topics become easier to understand when the author separates observation , interpretation , and decision
The chapter defines a working model
The distinction matters because the same evidence can support several plausible interpretations
The chapter also introduces a qualifier
Observation refers to what can be directly described
Interpretation refers to the meaning assigned to those descriptions
Decision refers to the action chosen after weighing competing interpretations
This model is simple, but it matters because it prevents people from acting as if every first impression is already a justified conclusion
The model is useful only if the reader is willing to state uncertainty explicitly
In practice, many decisions must still be made before certainty is available, so the goal is not perfect knowledge
